I wonder if devs would also exclude long running requests from metrics?

Would this affect the "http.server.active_requests" metric? If so, how would that work given that it's incremented before routing and the metric is tracked by the `IHttpApplication`? If not, would it be better to call this something like `[DisableRequestDurationMetrics]`?

`[DisableHttpMetrics]` sounds very broad. Is there anything other than the "http.server.request.duration" metric you could foresee us wanting to disable based on this metadata? If excluding requests from the "http.server.request.duration" metric is the primary motivator for this metadata as #50654 suggests, we wouldn't want to have people unintentionally opting out of getting other "http" metrics for that endpoint just because they didn't want warnings for long request durations.

Also, would we use this by default for relevant SignalR/Blazor endpoints? It seems safer to do if it just affects the request duration metric. @BrennanConroy
Also, the `IEndpointConventionBuilder` extension method should probably do the `TBuilder` thing for better chaining.

review_comments:
```suggestion
[AttributeUsage(AttributeTargets.Method | AttributeTargets.Class | AttributeTargets.Delegate)]
```

Do we want to support applying this attribute directly on a minimal API handler like so?

```csharp
app.MapGet("/", [DisableHttpMetrics] () => { });
```

Extension methods are the more common pattern for minimal APIs but some people still prefer the attribute.

Also, does this benefit from a `DebuggerDisplay` attribution?

I believe `AttributeTargets.Parameter` is what would allow this.

I'm going to leave it off because the parameter target is missing from most attributes. If this changes, it can be added everyone at once.

---

Good point about debugger display. Other metadata has some stuff here so I'll make this consistent.
What's the flag interface for?  Relatedly, if there's only one concrete implementation, can we just use that?
Using interfaces for endpoint metadata is the normal pattern. The only implementation is an attribute. Internally, builder methods that add this metadata to the endpoint just add the attribute.
Metrics noob question: why is `-1` the indicator that the metric is disabled here as opposed to the lack of a measurement point?

The disable metrics feature only disables `http.server.request.duration`. The active request counter (this one) is unchanged.

It goes up by 1 when the request starts and down by 1 when the request ends. You're seeing the result of the request ending.
